subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw accept YAML/YML as a second user config-file format, or keep JSON5 `openclaw.json` as the only config-file contract and improve the structured mutation path instead?
rationale: This changes the stable core config contract and compatibility/write semantics, so code inspection can show the current state but cannot decide the product tradeoff.

options.title: Keep JSON5-only
options.body: Keep `openclaw.json` as the canonical file and improve docs/tooling around `openclaw config` and `config.patch` for comment-aware scripted edits.

options.title: Design YAML support
options.body: Accept YAML only after specifying parser behavior, precedence, write/backup/doctor semantics, and upgrade tests for JSON and YAML installs.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: If maintainers do not want another config format, close this and point users to the CLI/RPC mutation path.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5-only
recommendation.body: Keep `openclaw.json` as the canonical file and improve docs/tooling around `openclaw config` and `config.patch` for comment-aware scripted edits.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent config docs/schema work and product-surface commits make this the best available owner signal for the product-direction call.
